example.title: Don't touch that Fan!
example.description: What do you expect will happen when you move your cursor on the fan? This is a very basic example visual force feedback. Click the icons above for other examples.

example.title: Pocket + Tunnel
example.description: Try and move your cursor through the tunnel, or in the pocket. Using dynamic forcefields to create different levels.

example.title: Menu with slick-disabled buttons
example.description: The disabled items in the drop-down menus are made slick, so that the cursor slides over them quickly. An example of assisted navigation.

example.title: Ball Game
example.description: Virtual version of the well known ball game requiring patience and coordination. Can you get the two balls in the two holes?

example.title: Cursor Bug
example.description: You are cursor bug flying in the room. Try to land it on his Nose! Created by Holland Interactive

example.title: Confirm Button
example.description: After clicking the Delete button – which initiates an unrecommended action – the system asks for a confirmation, whereby the cursor is pushed towards the 'no' button which cancels the action. An example of mixed initiative.

example.title: Windowbuttons
example.description: Those small buttons in the corner of windows can be difficult to click. Window A has buttons augmented with a force target, which drags the cursor to the center and makes them easier to click than the regular ones in window B. Scientific research points out that the usability of the augmented buttons is significantly higher. Do you notice the difference?

example.title: Block
example.description: The wooden cube can be flipped by pushing the cursor on the right side. This is a more complex example of how visual force feedback can be used to simulate properties of physical objects.

example.title: Maze
example.description: This simple maze example shows how to use a wall object.

example.title: Sweet Switch
example.description: Try and move your cursor through the tunnel, or in the pocket. Using dynamic forcefields to create different levels.
